claims.statement: OpenHands provides a unified, extensible platform for building AI agents that interact with computing environments through code execution, command-line access, and web browsing.
A Docker-sandboxed runtime prevents agent-generated code from affecting the host system, enabling safe evaluation and deployment.
CodeActAgent v1.8 with claude-3-5-sonnet achieves a 26.0% resolve rate on SWE-Bench Lite, comparable to open-source software-engineering specialists such as Aider (26.3%) and Moatless Tools (26.7%).
claims.scope: SWE-Bench Lite, 300 instances, without hint text, 0-shot

claims.statement: CodeActAgent (0-shot) achieves 79.3% on HumanEvalFix Python, substantially exceeding non-agentic code models (e.g., StarCoder2-15B at 48.6%), though below SWE-Agent's 1-shot result of 87.7%.
The same generalist CodeActAgent, without task-specific prompt modification, achieves competitive performance across software engineering, web browsing, and general assistance task categories.
claims.scope: Results span multiple benchmarks; generality claim is relative to task-specific baselines

claims.statement: CodeActAgent with tool use achieves 52.0% accuracy on the GPQA diamond benchmark, surpassing GPT-4 few-shot chain-of-thought (38.8%) and exceeding the non-expert human baseline (21.9%).
The event-stream abstraction decouples agent logic from environment details, enabling modular development and drop-in substitution of agent implementations.
Multi-agent delegation allows a generalist agent to hand off subtasks to specialists, demonstrated by CodeActAgent delegating web browsing to BrowsingAgent via AgentDelegateAction.
The platform integrates 15 benchmarks spanning software engineering, web interaction, and general assistance, supporting systematic evaluation of agent generality.
Current OpenHands agents underperform on long-file editing tasks and require substantial handcrafted workflow design, representing open engineering challenges.

limitations.description: Docker isolation reduces but does not eliminate risk from agent actions; network access and resource consumption remain potential concerns.
